review: All 11 methods use the same fixed paired PSR observations. Each method keeps its own first certified stop or cap-abstention prefix. The physical path continues until every method has an outcome.

The fine hedge consumes each original fine block. The coarse hedge aggregates exactly the first 16 physical pairs into one Fisher block at 32 shots, then uses the same later blocks. Its counts and sufficient statistics have the correct coarse distribution, without claiming the old runner RNG trajectory is reproduced.
The fine schedule equals every even shot through 32 plus the original schedule above 32. The coarse hedge is ineligible before 32; all later checked points coincide with its prescribed schedule.

The exact and seven generic boundary artifacts are hash-bound, verified, and matched by method name, delta=1/100 and D horizon=cap/2. Ville beta and both hedge procedures retain their original threshold-100 rules.

True probabilities occur only in the simulator closure and final scoring. Counts passed to certificates contain no true model parameter. Binomial draws generate the correct independent Bernoulli-pair joint categories.

The released case matrix has 16 main cases including sign mirrors, two null cases, 32 repetitions, 576 physical paths and 6336 method records. Every wrong stop and cap abstention is included in mean costs and equal-case ratios.

Run is blocked until an explicit root release binds the exact plan, source map, boundary map, passed independent review and deadlines. A partial observed prefix and its completed method outcomes are flushed before an interrupted run stops.

Reproduced deterministic bookkeeping checks: coarse aggregation, distinct stopped prefixes, active-method removal, deadline preservation, invalid observed counts and complete-matrix summary checks all pass without RNG.

synthetic_checks.scope: Deterministic bookkeeping only; zero simulator observations

limits: This is source and deterministic bookkeeping review, not completion of the future generated-data audit.
The case set is a development comparison. It supplies no held-out superiority claim, inferential confidence interval or empirical certification of 1% error.
At cap 4096 the closed-hedge labels denote the old PSR warm-up behavior; actual closed-angle adaptation is not exercised.
Finite-cap tests exploit the known budget, whereas the original Ville and hedge rules supply unrestricted-horizon guarantees. This distinction must remain explicit.
Each method is an individually valid test. The benchmark records them separately and does not create a combined stop-at-any-method decision rule.
Shared CPU timings are not standalone per-method computational costs.
